reasons: No tests are included for this file.
Overrides many library class names, so it depends on the library version staying compatible.

terms.meaning: a control that lets a user choose a date from a visual calendar
a span of consecutive days, from a start day to an end day
the language and regional format settings of the user's browser

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the calendar
sections.what: Loads the calendar library, the arrow icons and the shared button. Nothing is shown on its own.
sections.why: Lets the file build on the library instead of writing a calendar from scratch.
sections.watch_out: The shared button file must exist at its expected path or the calendar will not load.

sections.name: Calendar (part 1)
sections.title: Main settings and layout look (part 1)
sections.what: Sets default options such as showing days from neighboring months and a plain text month label. It then sets the look of the main layout, the arrows, the month title, and the month and year pickers.
sections.why: Adds the app's look on top of the library's defaults.
sections.watch_out: Month names in the picker use the browser language, which may not match the rest of the app.

sections.name: Calendar (part 2)
sections.title: Day, week and state looks (part 2)
sections.what: Sets the look of the weekday headings, the week rows, individual days, range highlights, today's date, days from other months, and disabled days. Class names passed by the page are applied last and win.
sections.why: Lets selected ranges and today's date look distinct from other days.
sections.watch_out: Because the page's own class names are applied last, a page can override these highlights without editing this file.

sections.name: Calendar (part 3)
sections.title: Custom arrows, outer box and week numbers (part 3)
sections.what: Replaces some library pieces with the app's own: the outer box, the up, down, left and right arrows, the day button, and the week number column.
sections.why: Lets the arrows and week numbers match the icons used elsewhere in the app.
sections.watch_out: Parts the page passes in are applied last and replace these entirely rather than merging with them.

sections.name: CalendarDayButton
sections.title: Single day button
sections.what: Draws one day as a plain ghost button. It is highlighted when selected, when inside a range, or when it is a range start or end. It also moves keyboard focus onto the day when navigated with the keyboard.
sections.why: Keeps each day clear to see and usable with a keyboard.
sections.watch_out: The day's data label uses the browser's date text format, which depends on language settings and can break code that expects a fixed format.

summary: A month calendar for picking a single day or a range of days, with styled days, arrows and month and year pickers.
purpose: Lets a user choose dates from a calendar grid rather than typing them.
why: Likely reason: built on the react-day-picker library, with the app's look added on top. Reason not stated for specific style choices.
how: Step 1: Loads the calendar library, the arrow icons and the shared button. Step 2: Sets the main calendar options and the look of the layout, arrows and month title. Step 3: Sets the look of weekday headings, days and highlights. Step 4: Replaces some default parts with the app's own, such as the arrows and week numbers. Step 5: Draws each day as a button that shows selection and keyboard focus.
inputs: Calendar settings from the library, such as the selected date or range, plus optional style classes, replacement parts and a button style.
outputs: A calendar on screen. Clicking a day reports the selection to the page through the library.
risks: Month and day names use the browser language setting, so the output can differ from user to user. The file overrides many internal class names of the library, so a library update can break the look.
debug: If the look is wrong after an update, check that the library's default class names still exist. If month or day names appear in an unexpected language, check the browser language. If a day does not respond, check the disabled settings the page passes in.
